usage.main:
Usage:
  ulgen            sign in, pick a tool, set it up and start it
  ulgen <tool>     the same for one tool: qwen, opencode, codex, claude

  ulgen login      sign in to EVREN: opens the API keys page, saves the key, records that you accepted the terms
  ulgen logout     remove the saved key
  ulgen status     remaining daily quota and models
  ulgen doctor     check the key, EVREN and the tools; say what to do about what is wrong
  ulgen setup      set up coding tools for EVREN (qwen, opencode, codex, claude)
  ulgen run        start a tool with the key in its environment; Claude Code through the translator

Advanced:
  ulgen worker     run one headless Claude Code on an EVREN model to do a task unattended
  ulgen proxy      run the translator on its own, for a program that speaks the Anthropic API
  ulgen token      print the saved key for another program
  ulgen version    print the version

Run "ulgen <command> -h" for a command's options.

setup.usage:
Usage:
  ulgen setup                       list the tools and their state
  ulgen setup <tool>... [options]   set up the named tools (%s)
  ulgen setup all [options]         set up every supported tool that is installed
  ulgen setup --remove <tool>...    undo what setup wrote for the named tools (or all)

Options:
setup.all_alone: "all" cannot be combined with tool names
setup.options_need_tool: options were given without a tool; name the tools to set up (%s) or use "all"
setup.none_installed: none of the supported tools is installed (%s); install one, or name a tool to set it up before it is installed
setup.unknown_model: EVREN has no tool-capable chat model named %[1]s; choose one of: %[2]s
setup.no_models: EVREN lists no chat model with tool support
setup.models_skipped.one: %d model was left out (unusual name, no context size, or a repeated id)
setup.models_skipped.other: %d models were left out (unusual name, no context size, or a repeated id)
setup.base_url_note: note: the tools are pointed at %s, not at EVREN; your key will be sent there
setup.backup_holds_key: the old file held your API key in clear text; the backup at %s still holds it
setup.file_holds_key: your API key is still in the new file, in clear text, on line %s; Ülgen does not remove it
setup.file_holds_key_lines: your API key is still in the new file, in clear text, on lines %s; Ülgen does not remove it
setup.up_to_date: already set up; nothing to change
setup.dry_run_hidden: the change is in a value that is not shown
flag.setup_remove: undo what setup wrote for the named tools; the key and the network are not needed
setup.remove_alone: --remove goes with the tools and --dry-run only
setup.remove.done: EVREN is no longer set up in %s.
setup.list.hint: Set a tool up with:  ulgen setup <tool>
setup.note.export: To start it by its own name, put the key in your shell first:  %s
setup.note.default_kept: %[1]s keeps its own default model. Pick an EVREN model inside it, or run:  ulgen setup %[2]s --default
setup.note.default_replaced: The default model was "%[1]s", which is not among the EVREN models ulgen sets up; ulgen sets %[2]s instead.
setup.note.small_replaced: The model for titles (small_model) was "%[1]s", which is not among the EVREN models ulgen sets up; ulgen sets %[2]s instead.
setup.note.qwen_env_default: Qwen Code takes its default model from the environment (%[1]s), so ulgen selected no EVREN model. To make EVREN the default run:  ulgen setup %[2]s --default
setup.note.qwen_entry_removed: ulgen removes the entry "%[1]s" (baseUrl "%[2]s") from modelProviders.openai: it reads EVREN_API_KEY and is not one of EVREN's models. The file as it was goes to the backup; an entry of your own needs a variable of its own in envKey.
setup.note.stats_off: Usage statistics were switched off (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled); Qwen Code sends them to a third party.
setup.note.stats_off_planned: Usage statistics would be switched off (privacy.usageStatisticsEnabled); Qwen Code sends them to a third party.
setup.note.remove_copy: %s holds a copy of the EVREN entry; Ülgen does not write that file, so the entry is still there.
setup.note.qwen_home_file: %s sets QWEN_HOME, so Qwen Code uses another directory than the one ulgen set up. Remove that line, or run ulgen setup qwen with QWEN_HOME set to the same directory.
setup.note.trailing_comma: %s has a trailing comma, which Qwen Code does not accept; remove it.
setup.note.node_old: Qwen Code needs Node.js 22 or newer; this machine has %s.
setup.note.node_missing: Qwen Code needs Node.js 22 or newer; none was found.
setup.note.opencode_copy: %[1]s holds an EVREN provider of ulgen's as well. opencode reads it together with %[2]s, and ulgen no longer keeps that copy up to date; remove provider.evren from %[1]s.
setup.note.opencode_home_copy: %s holds an EVREN provider of ulgen's. ulgen does not keep that copy up to date, and "ulgen run opencode" takes that file for a project file and will not start opencode while it names the key; remove provider.evren from it.
setup.note.opencode_set_above: %[1]s sets %[2]s, and opencode reads that file over the one ulgen writes: ulgen did not write %[2]s. To use EVREN's, set it to "%[3]s" in that file.
setup.note.opencode_key_replaced: ulgen replaces options.apiKey of provider.evren in %s with {env:EVREN_API_KEY}; the file as it was goes to the backup.
setup.note.opencode_models_dropped: ulgen drops from provider.evren.models in %[2]s what is not among EVREN's models: %[1]s. The file as it was goes to the backup.
setup.note.opencode_disabled: %s lists evren under disabled_providers, so opencode will not use the EVREN models; take it off that list.
setup.note.opencode_not_enabled: %s has an enabled_providers list without evren, so opencode will not use the EVREN models; add "evren" to that list.
setup.note.opencode_native: %s defines providers.evren, the form opencode 2 reads first: it takes the place of the provider.evren ulgen writes. Remove or rename it.
setup.note.opencode_config_var: OPENCODE_CONFIG is set: opencode also reads the file it names, and ulgen does not look at that file. A default model or a provider named evren in that file can take precedence over what ulgen has written.
setup.note.codex_profile: EVREN is a profile in Codex; by its own name it starts with:  codex --profile evren
setup.note.codex_rewritten: Comments and the layout of %[1]s are not kept (the order of the keys, the way strings and numbers are written, inline tables): ulgen writes the file anew when one of its settings changes. Every value of your other settings stays, and the file as it was goes to the backup.
setup.note.codex_model_replaced: The profile named the model "%[1]s", which is not among the EVREN models ulgen can set up; ulgen sets %[2]s instead.
setup.note.codex_followed_model: %s follows the new model: the value the profile held for the model before is not kept.
setup.note.codex_default: --default does not apply to Codex: its own default stays, and EVREN is the profile.
setup.install.opencode: Install it with:  npm install -g opencode-ai
setup.err.parse: %[1]s is not valid %[2]s (%[3]s); fix it or move it away, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.shape: %[1]s is not laid out as expected (%[2]s); fix it or move it away, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.foreign: %[1]s defines %[2]s, an entry that is not ulgen's; ulgen does not overwrite it and cannot set EVREN up under the same name next to it; remove or rename it, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.default_clash: %[1]s names "%[2]s" as Qwen Code's default model, and no entry under modelProviders has that id. EVREN offers a model of that name, so once EVREN is set up Qwen Code would start on EVREN's entry instead of yours. To make EVREN the default, run ulgen setup qwen --default; to keep your own, add an entry for your model under modelProviders.openai first
setup.err.legacy_profile: %[1]s has %[2]s, the old way to select or define a profile, and Codex cannot use a profile file such as evren.config.toml while it is there; remove it (settings you want to keep go into a profile file of their own, NAME.config.toml, which codex --profile NAME uses), then run ulgen setup codex again
setup.err.missing_dir: %[1]s points to %[2]s, which does not exist
setup.err.var_not_dir: %[1]s points to %[2]s, which is not a directory
setup.err.is_dir: %s is a directory where a file is expected; move it away, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.not_dir: %s is not a directory, and a directory is expected there; move it away, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.request: the setup request is not usable: %s
setup.err.changed: %s changed while setup was working; nothing was written to it, run ulgen setup again
setup.err.read_only: %s is read-only and was left as it is; make it writable, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.link: the symbolic link at %s points to a file that does not exist; repair or remove the link, then run ulgen setup again
setup.err.backup_exists: a backup of %[1]s from an earlier run is already at %[2]s and differs; nothing was written to %[1]s, and running ulgen setup again a moment later uses a new backup directory
setup.err.backup_made: the file as it was is saved at %s
setup.err.backup_dir: the backup directory could not be prepared: %s
run.usage:
Usage:
  ulgen run [options] <tool> [arguments...]

Starts the tool with the EVREN key in its environment. Everything after the tool's name goes to the tool unchanged. Claude Code is started through a translator on this machine and does not get the key. On Windows a tool whose .cmd file is not the one npm writes is started through cmd.exe, and then an argument that contains one of " %% ^ ! or a control character, or a command line longer than 8191 characters, is refused.
Tools: %s

Options:
run.not_set_up: EVREN is not set up in %[1]s; run ulgen setup %[2]s
run.shim_arg: argument %[1]d contains %[2]s, which cannot be passed safely to a tool that Windows starts through cmd.exe; %[3]s can be started without that argument
run.shim_arg_newline: argument %[1]d contains a line break, which cannot be passed safely to a tool that Windows starts through cmd.exe; %[2]s can be started without that argument
run.shim_path: the path of %[1]s, %[2]s, contains %[3]s, so Windows cannot start it safely through cmd.exe; install the tool in a directory without that character
run.shim_line_too_long: the arguments make a command line longer than the %[1]d characters Windows allows, so %[2]s cannot be started through cmd.exe; pass fewer or shorter arguments
run.project_file: %[1]s names the EVREN key or the EVREN provider. A file of the project can send your key to another address, so %[2]s was not started. To start it anyway:  ulgen run --trust-project %[3]s
run.project_file_reference: %[1]s takes part of its settings from another file ({file:…}), which ulgen does not check; that part can name the EVREN provider or carry your key to another address, so %[2]s was not started. To start it anyway:  ulgen run --trust-project %[3]s
run.project_unreadable: %[1]s is a project file of %[2]s that could not be read, so it is not known whether it sends your key to another address; %[2]s was not started. To start it anyway:  ulgen run --trust-project %[3]s
run.project_unchecked: the files of the project could not be checked (%[1]s), so the tool was not started. To start it anyway:  ulgen run --trust-project %[2]s
run.claude_notice: Claude Code runs on an EVREN model through Ülgen's translator; Anthropic does not support this use.
run.options_need_proxied: --model and --base-url apply only to %s, which Ülgen starts through the translator
flag.proxy_port: the port to listen on (0: the system picks a free one)
flag.proxy_print_env: print the lines that point a shell at the translator (the token is printed in full)
proxy.token_short: %[1]s is shorter than %[2]d characters; set a longer token or unset it
proxy.token_failed: a token could not be generated: %s
proxy.serve_stopped: the translator stopped serving while the tool is still running: %s
proxy.shutdown_failed: the translator could not be shut down: %s
flag.worker_dir: the directory the worker runs in (default: the working directory); a project, not the home directory or a file system root
flag.worker_allow: allow more than the default rules: a permission rule, or one of the presets %s (may be repeated)
flag.worker_timeout: end the worker after this long (0: no timeout)
flag.worker_max_turns: give Claude Code --max-turns with this value (default: unlimited)
flag.worker_out: write the worker's JSON output (its whole answer) to this file
flag.worker_no_sandbox: do not turn on Claude Code's own sandbox (do not use this with a worker you do not trust)
worker.usage:
Usage:
  ulgen worker [options] <task-file | ->

Runs one headless Claude Code on an EVREN model to do the task in the file (or on standard input for -) unattended, in --dir, with the given allow-list, and prints a short summary. Claude Code reaches EVREN through Ülgen's translator on this machine; it never sees the EVREN key. Presets for --allow: %s.

Options:
worker.no_task: name the task file, or - to read the task from standard input
worker.allow_shape: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s is not one permission rule (the form is Name or Name(…), on one line, with no comma and no further parenthesis inside)
worker.allow_tool: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s names no tool the worker knows; the tools are Bash, Read, WebFetch and WebSearch
worker.allow_edit: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s is a rule for an editing tool; a worker already edits files under its directory, and a rule cannot widen that (give a wider --dir instead)
worker.allow_operator: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s holds a character that joins or redirects shell commands (; & | < > or a backquote); a rule names one command
worker.allow_bash_spec: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s is a Bash rule without a command specifier; a Bash rule needs one, as in Bash(make test:*)
worker.allow_any_bash: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s would let the worker run any shell command; the allow-list is the worker's fence, so it is refused (allow the commands the task needs one by one)
worker.allow_runner: the %[1]s --allow value %[2]s is a rule for a shell or a command runner, which would allow everything; give the commands the task needs one by one
worker.task_unreadable: the task %[1]s could not be read: %[2]s
worker.task_too_large: the task is larger than %s; keep it to what the worker must do
worker.task_empty: the task is empty; write what the worker is to do
worker.dir_cwd: the working directory could not be found: %s
worker.dir_home: --dir %s is your home directory; a worker edits files without asking, so point it at a project, not at everything
worker.dir_home_parent: --dir %s holds your home directory; a worker edits files without asking, so point it at a project, not at everything
worker.dir_root: --dir %s is a file system root; a worker edits files without asking, so point it at a project, not at everything
worker.out_failed: the worker's output could not be written to %[1]s: %[2]s
worker.denials: %d tool calls were refused by the worker's permissions
worker.output_too_large: the worker wrote more than %s of output; it was stopped
worker.no_sandbox_windows: on this system a worker's shell commands cannot be confined; --no-sandbox accepts that; Claude Code's sandbox works under WSL2
worker.no_sandbox: the worker's shell commands are not confined to its directory
setup.note.claude_not_supported: Anthropic does not support running Claude Code against another provider; it is started through Ülgen's translator and reaches EVREN that way.
setup.note.skill_foreign: %s is your own skill; it was left as it is.
setup.note.skill_foreign_planned: %s is your own skill; it would be left as it is.
token.terminal: this would print your API key on the screen; add --show if you mean it
token.write_failed: the key could not be written to the output: %s
